name: Partial computable function
description: A partial function on the naturals whose graph is the set of input-output pairs realized by some Turing machine (defined exactly where the machine halts).

name: Total computable function
description: A total function on the naturals computed by a Turing machine that halts on every input.

name: Primitive recursion schema
description: The function-building rule defining f(x,0)=g(x) and f(x,n+1)=h(x,n,f(x,n)), one of the closure operations generating the primitive recursive functions.

name: μ-operator (unbounded minimization)
description: The search operator producing g(x)=the least y with f(x,y)=0 (undefined if none exists), whose addition to the primitive recursive base yields exactly the partial recursive functions.

name: Partial recursive functions
description: The smallest class of partial functions containing the basic functions (zero, successor, projections) and closed under composition, primitive recursion, and the μ-operator.

name: Register machine
description: An abstract computing device with finitely many unbounded-integer registers manipulated by increment/decrement-and-jump instructions, an alternative model defining exactly the computable functions.

name: Church–Turing Thesis
description: The informal claim that every function effectively calculable by an algorithm is computable by a Turing machine (equivalently, is partial recursive).

name: Computability Thesis (Soare)
description: Soare's reformulation asserting that the intuitively computable functions coincide with the Turing-computable functions, motivating the terminology 'computable/c.e.' in place of 'recursive'.

name: Oracle Turing machine
description: A Turing machine equipped with a query tape that may consult an oracle set A for membership answers during its computation, the device underlying relative computability.

name: Use function
description: The function u(e,x,s) giving the largest oracle argument queried during the halting computation of Φ_e^A(x) (by stage s), bounding which oracle bits affect the output.

name: Gödel number / index
description: A natural number coding a Turing machine (or partial recursive program) under a fixed effective enumeration, so that e is an index for the e-th partial computable function φ_e.

name: Turing jump A′
description: The halting set relativized to oracle A, A′={e : Φ_e^A(e)↓}, the canonical operator strictly raising Turing degree.

name: Arithmetical hierarchy
description: The classification of subsets of ℕ by the number of alternating number quantifiers prefixing a computable matrix, with Σ0_n existential-leading, Π0_n universal-leading, and Δ0_n their intersection.

name: Many-one (m) reducibility
description: A≤_m B iff there is a total computable f with x∈A ⟺ f(x)∈B for all x.

name: One-one (1) reducibility
description: A≤_1 B iff there is a total computable injection f with x∈A ⟺ f(x)∈B for all x.

name: Truth-table (tt) reducibility
description: A≤_tt B iff there is a total computable procedure assigning to each x a finite Boolean truth-table condition on B-membership of finitely many points that decides x∈A (a total, hence everywhere-converging, Turing reduction).

name: Weak truth-table (wtt) reducibility
description: A≤_wtt B iff A≤_T B via an oracle reduction whose use is bounded by a computable function of the input.

name: Simple set
description: A c.e. set whose complement is infinite yet contains no infinite c.e. subset (Post's first weakening of completeness).

name: Immune set
description: An infinite set containing no infinite computably enumerable subset.

name: Productive set
description: A set A with a total computable productive function p such that whenever W_e⊆A then p(e)∈A∖W_e, witnessing that A is not c.e. in an effective way.

name: Creative set
description: A computably enumerable set whose complement is productive; equivalently a many-one complete c.e. set such as K.

name: Diagonal halting set K0
description: The set K0={⟨e,x⟩ : Φ_e(x)↓} of pairs encoding a machine and an input on which it halts, a c.e. many-one complete set.

name: Hypersimple set
description: A c.e. set whose complement is hyperimmune, i.e. its principal (enumeration-ordered) function is not dominated by any computable function.

name: Hyperimmune set
description: An infinite set whose principal function (listing its elements in increasing order) is not majorized by any computable function.

name: Hyperhypersimple set
description: A c.e. set whose complement cannot be covered by any uniformly computable array of finite sets meeting it in exactly one block each (strengthening hypersimplicity).

name: Maximal set
description: A c.e. set whose complement is infinite and cannot be split into two infinite pieces by any c.e. set, i.e. it is a coatom in the lattice of c.e. sets modulo finite difference.

name: Stage approximation Φ_{e,s}^A(x)
description: The s-step truncation of the oracle computation Φ_e^A(x), which converges iff the full computation halts within s stages, providing the computable approximations used in priority constructions.

name: Enumeration Theorem
description: There is a single partial computable function (universal function) that, given an index e and input x, simulates φ_e(x).

name: Kleene Normal Form Theorem
description: Every partial computable function can be written as U(μs.T(e,x,s)) for a fixed primitive recursive Kleene T-predicate and primitive recursive output U, using a single application of the μ-operator.

name: c.e. = Σ0_1 characterization
description: A set is computably enumerable iff it is the domain of a partial computable function iff it is the projection of a computable relation iff it is definable by a single existential number quantifier over a computable matrix.
aliases: Σ01 normal form for c.e. sets

name: Post's Complementation Theorem
type_signature: A computable ⟺ A and ℕ∖A both c.e.
description: A set is computable (decidable) if and only if both it and its complement are computably enumerable.
aliases: Post's theorem (computable iff c.e. and co-c.e.)

name: Recursion Theorem with parameters
description: A uniform (parametrized) version of Kleene's recursion theorem producing a computable function of the parameters that returns fixed-point indices uniformly.

name: Myhill Isomorphism Theorem
type_signature: A≤_1 B ∧ B≤_1 A ⟹ A≡ B (computable permutation)
description: Two sets that are one-one reducible to each other are computably isomorphic, i.e. there is a computable permutation of ℕ carrying one onto the other.

name: Myhill characterization of creative sets
description: The creative sets are exactly the many-one complete c.e. sets, and all are computably isomorphic to the halting set K.

name: m-completeness of K
description: Every computably enumerable set many-one reduces to the halting set K, so K is m-complete (indeed 1-complete) among c.e. sets.

name: Jump Theorem
type_signature: A<_T A′; A≤_T B ⟹ A′≤_m B′; A′ is Σ0_1(A)-complete
description: The Turing jump satisfies A<_T A′ strictly, is monotone (A≤_T B implies A′≤_m B′ hence A′≤_T B′), and A′ is c.e. in and complete for A.

name: Post's Theorem
description: Connects the arithmetical hierarchy to iterated jumps: a set is Σ0_{n+1} iff it is c.e. in the n-th jump 0^{(n)}, and Δ0_{n+1} comprises exactly the sets Turing-below 0^{(n)}.

name: Hierarchy Theorem (arithmetical hierarchy is proper)
description: For every n the arithmetical hierarchy is strict, with Σ0_n, Π0_n, and Δ0_n all distinct, witnessed by the n-th jump.

name: Shoenfield Limit Lemma
type_signature: A≤_T 0′ ⟺ A(x)=lim_s g(x,s) for computable g
description: A set (or function) is Turing reducible to 0′ if and only if it is the pointwise limit of a computable sequence of approximations; equivalently A is Δ0_2.

name: Modulus Lemma
type_signature: A≤_T ∅′ with c.e. approx ⟹ ∃ modulus m≤_T A
description: If A has a computable approximation converging to a Δ0_2 set, then any function dominating its modulus of convergence computes A; in particular every c.e. set has a modulus of its enumeration of the same Turing degree.

name: Existence of a simple set (Post)
description: Post constructed a computably enumerable set that is simple, hence c.e., noncomputable, and not many-one complete, advancing toward Post's problem.

name: Productive sets are not c.e.
description: A productive set cannot be computably enumerable, since its productive function effectively escapes every candidate enumeration W_e⊆A.

name: Relativization principle
type_signature: Theorem(∅) ⟹ Theorem(A) for all oracles A
description: The meta-principle that results proved about computable functions and c.e. sets remain valid uniformly when all notions are relativized to an arbitrary oracle A.

name: Dovetailing
function_signature: (countably many computations) → (single fair interleaved enumeration)
description: A scheduling method that runs infinitely many partial computations together by advancing each one finitely at successive stages, ensuring every computation that halts is eventually seen.

function_signature: (ℕ×ℕ) → ℕ
name: Pairing function / coding of tuples
description: A computable bijection ⟨·,·⟩:ℕ²→ℕ (e.g. Cantor's polynomial) with computable inverses, extended to code finite tuples and sequences as single numbers.

function_signature: (requirement list) → (set built by stages with movable markers)
name: Construction by stages with movable markers
description: A method that builds a c.e. set or function in stages, tracking the current candidate witness for each requirement by a marker that is moved (released) when its requirement is reinjured or refined.

name: Permitting method
function_signature: (c.e. set C, requirement) → (object ≤_T C built only when C permits)
description: A construction technique that makes a built set computable in a given c.e. set C by only acting on a requirement at a stage when C newly enumerates a small element ('permits' the change).

name: Reduction to K (proving undecidability)
function_signature: (problem P) → (m-reduction K≤_m P proving P undecidable)
description: A proof method establishing undecidability of a set P by exhibiting a computable many-one reduction from the halting set K (or another known undecidable set) to P.

name: Computable approximation (Δ0_2 method)
function_signature: (Δ0_2 object A) → (computable sequence A_s with lim_s A_s = A)
description: The technique of representing a Δ0_2 set or function as the limit of a computable stagewise approximation, the workhorse behind Limit-Lemma and injury constructions.

name: Turing equivalence (≡_T)
description: The equivalence relation A≡_T B holding when A≤_T B and B≤_T A, i.e. each set computes the other.

name: Turing degree
description: An equivalence class of subsets of ℕ under Turing equivalence, representing a level of relative computability.

name: Degree structure D
description: The upper semilattice of all Turing degrees partially ordered by relative computability, with least element 0, join operation, and the jump operator.

name: Join of degrees (a∨b)
description: The least upper bound of two Turing degrees, computed by the degree of the disjoint sum A⊕B={2x:x∈A}∪{2x+1:x∈B}.

name: Degree 0
description: The least Turing degree, consisting precisely of the computable (decidable) sets.

name: Degree 0′ (zero jump)
description: The Turing degree of the halting problem, the jump of 0 and the greatest c.e. degree.

name: Jump hierarchy (0,0′,0″,…)
description: The strictly increasing sequence of iterated jumps of 0, giving canonical representatives 0^{(n)} of degrees high in the arithmetical hierarchy.

name: c.e. degrees R
description: The substructure of Turing degrees containing a computably enumerable set, an upper semilattice with least element 0 and greatest element 0′.

name: Low set / degree
description: A set (or degree) whose jump is as low as possible, A′≡_T 0′, so it computes nothing extra at the jump level.

name: Low_n degree
description: A degree whose n-th jump equals 0^{(n)}, generalizing lowness to higher jumps.

name: High set / degree
description: A degree below 0′ whose jump is as high as possible, A′≡_T 0″, so it computes a function dominating all computable functions.

name: High_n degree
description: A degree below 0′ whose n-th jump is maximal, A^{(n)}≡_T 0^{(n+1)}.

name: High/Low hierarchy
description: The classification of c.e. (or Δ0_2) degrees by how their iterated jumps compare to the corresponding jumps of 0, forming nested Low_n and High_n classes.

name: Superlow degree
description: A degree whose jump is truth-table (not merely Turing) equivalent to 0′, a uniform strengthening of lowness.

name: Hyperimmune-free degree
type_signature: a≠0 with every f≤_T a dominated by a computable g
description: A nonzero degree every function of which is majorized by a computable function (equivalently, every f≤_T a is computably dominated).

name: Hyperimmune degree
type_signature: a computing a function dominating no computable g
description: A degree that computes a function not majorized by any computable function (i.e. computes a hyperimmune set's principal function).

name: GL1 degree (generalized low 1)
description: A degree satisfying the generalized lowness condition a′≡_T a∨0′, the relativized analogue of lowness not requiring a≤_T 0′.

name: GL2 degree (generalized low 2)
description: A degree satisfying a″≡_T (a∨0′)′; the complement GL2̄ (a not GL2) marks degrees of strong domination/escape properties.

name: Minimal degree
description: A nonzero Turing degree with no degree strictly between it and 0, an atom of the degree ordering.

name: 1-generic set / degree
type_signature: G meeting/avoiding every Σ0_1 set of conditions
description: A set G that is Cohen-generic for one-quantifier (Σ0_1) conditions: for each c.e. set of strings, G either meets it or has an initial segment with no extension in it.

name: n-generic set / degree
description: A set generic for arithmetical conditions of complexity Σ0_n, refining 1-genericity up the hierarchy.

name: Ershov hierarchy
description: The fine classification of Δ0_2 sets by the number (and ordinal type) of mind-changes allowed in a computable approximation, with the finite levels being the n-c.e. sets.

name: n-c.e. set
description: A set admitting a computable approximation A_s that changes its decision on each x at most n times (1-c.e. = c.e.).

name: d.c.e. set / degree
description: A difference of two computably enumerable sets (the 2-c.e. sets), and the degrees they realize.

name: e-state
type_signature: finite binary string over requirements R_0..R_{e}
description: In the maximal/dense-set constructions, the binary vector recording which of the first e c.e. sets a given element currently belongs to, maximized to push the construction toward a coatom complement.

name: Post's Problem
description: The question, solved affirmatively by Friedberg and Muchnik, of whether there exists a computably enumerable set whose Turing degree is strictly between 0 and 0′.

name: Kleene–Post Theorem
description: There exist Turing degrees a and b below 0′ that are incomparable, constructed by the finite extension method (though not necessarily c.e.).

name: Existence of incomparable c.e. degrees
description: There are computably enumerable sets of incomparable Turing degree, the content of the Friedberg–Muchnik solution to Post's problem realized within R.

name: Low Basis Theorem (Jockusch–Soare)
type_signature: every nonempty Π0_1 class has a low member
description: Every nonempty Π0_1 class (e.g. the paths of an infinite computable binary tree) contains a member of low Turing degree.

name: Hyperimmune-free Basis Theorem
type_signature: every nonempty Π0_1 class has a hyperimmune-free member
description: Every nonempty Π0_1 class contains a member of hyperimmune-free (computably dominated) degree.

name: Minimal Pair Theorem (Lachlan–Yates)
description: There exist nonzero computably enumerable degrees a and b whose only common lower bound is 0, a minimal pair in R.

name: Existence of a minimal degree (Spector)
description: Spector proved, by forcing with computable perfect trees, that minimal Turing degrees exist.

name: Exact Pair Theorem
type_signature: ideal I countable ⟹ ∃ a,b with I={c:c≤a ∧ c≤b}
description: Every countable ideal of Turing degrees has an exact pair: two degrees whose set of common lower bounds is exactly that ideal.

name: Embedding lattices into the c.e. degrees
description: Every finite (indeed countable) distributive lattice embeds, preserving join and meet, into the upper semilattice of computably enumerable degrees.

name: Nondistributivity of the c.e. degrees (Lachlan)
type_signature: R is not a distributive lattice
description: Lachlan showed the c.e. degrees fail distributivity by embedding the nonmodular/nondistributive five-element lattices, so R is not a distributive lattice.

name: Nondiamond Theorem (Lachlan)
type_signature: the four-element Boolean lattice does not embed into R preserving 0 and 1
description: Lachlan proved that the diamond lattice cannot be embedded into the c.e. degrees preserving both least and greatest elements (0 and 0′).

name: Robinson Low Splitting / interpolation
type_signature: low c.e. degrees split below any c.e. degree with interpolation
description: Robinson's theorem providing splitting of c.e. degrees by low c.e. degrees together with an interpolation/density property, refining Sacks splitting with lowness control.

name: Friedberg Jump Inversion Theorem
type_signature: ∀ c≥0′ ∃ a with a′≡_T a∨0′≡_T c
description: For every degree c≥0′ there is a degree a whose jump is c (and a∨0′=c), so the jump operator maps onto the cone above 0′.

name: Finite-injury priority method
function_signature: (priority-ranked requirement list) → (c.e. set/degree, each requirement injured finitely often)
description: A stagewise construction satisfying ranked requirements R_0,R_1,… in which lower-priority requirements may injure higher ones only finitely often, so each is eventually permanently satisfied.

name: Priority requirements and injury
function_signature: (competing requirements) → (priority ordering + injury bookkeeping)
description: The bookkeeping framework assigning a fixed priority order to requirements and declaring a requirement 'injured' when a higher-priority action undoes its current strategy, forcing it to restart.

name: Kleene–Post finite extension method
function_signature: (requirements) → (set built by finite initial-segment extensions, oracle 0′)
description: A forcing-style construction building characteristic functions by successive finite extensions, each diagonalizing one requirement, with the whole construction computable in 0′.

name: Length-of-agreement function
function_signature: (Φ_e^A, B, s) → ℓ(e,s)
description: The measure ℓ(e,s) of the longest initial segment on which a candidate reduction Φ_e^A agrees with target B at stage s, used to detect when a requirement appears satisfied.

name: Restraint function
function_signature: (requirement, stage) → ℕ
description: A function r(e,s) imposing a stagewise lower bound below which a strategy protects its computations, preventing lower-priority requirements from enumerating small elements that would injure it.

name: Hat trick
function_signature: (true-stage enumeration) → (corrected ('hatted') approximation Â_s)
description: A bookkeeping device in infinite-injury arguments that replaces A_s by the 'hatted' approximation reflecting only changes below the current restraint at true stages, taming nonmonotone injury.

name: Infinite-injury priority method
function_signature: (requirements possibly injured ∞ often along a tree) → (construction guided by the true path)
description: A priority construction in which requirements may be injured infinitely often, organized on a tree of strategies so that along the true path each requirement is met.

name: Tree of strategies
function_signature: (requirement guesses) → (tree of nodes, true path)
description: A tree whose nodes are strategy versions parametrized by finitely many guesses about the outcomes of higher-priority requirements, with the correct guesses lying on the true path.

name: True path
type_signature: infinite branch of the strategy tree
description: The leftmost path through the tree of strategies visited infinitely often, along which every requirement's correct guesses are realized.

name: Thickness Lemma
function_signature: (c.e. set A piecewise-thick over columns) → (B≤_T A built thick on required columns)
description: A lemma/technique in infinite-injury constructions guaranteeing a built c.e. set contains 'thick' (cofinite) portions of prescribed columns of a given set, used to control its degree.

name: Pinball machine
function_signature: (elements as balls + gates by priority) → (controlled enumeration into target)
description: A visualization/technique for 0‴ and density constructions in which elements ('balls') roll past priority-ordered 'gates' that hold or release them, regulating when they enter the constructed set.

name: 0‴-priority argument
function_signature: (requirements with two-level infinite injury) → (construction verified using 0‴)
description: A higher-level priority construction whose verification requires three jumps of bookkeeping (a tree-of-trees), e.g. in Lachlan's nondistributivity and density refinements.

name: Minimal pair construction
function_signature: (two c.e. sets A,B) → (common computations preserved so any C≤A,≤B is computable)
description: The technique of building two c.e. sets while preserving, for each potential common reduction, agreement that forces any set computable from both to be computable.

name: Spector's construction (tree forcing)
function_signature: (nested computable perfect trees) → (minimal-degree real on the intersection)
description: A forcing construction with a descending sequence of computable perfect (Spector) trees, each splitting or forcing total/partial behavior, yielding a real of minimal degree.

name: Cohen forcing in arithmetic
function_signature: (finite conditions / dense sets for arithmetic formulas) → (n-generic real)
description: The use of finite binary strings as Cohen forcing conditions to build generic reals deciding arithmetical statements, producing n-generic sets and degrees.
